questions.title: Politeness
questions.text: What did you do to show your politeness as a child?
questions.english: I used to greet adults and say thank you when someone helped me. Those were simple habits, but they were an easy way to show respect.
questions.chinese: 我以前会向长辈问好，也会在别人帮我时说谢谢。这些习惯很简单，却是表达尊重的容易方式。

questions.title: Politeness
questions.text: On what occasions should we be polite?

questions.title: 有条理的人
questions.text:
Describe a person you know who is very organized
You should say:
Who this person is
What this person usually does to stay organized
In what situations you have noticed this quality
And explain why you think being organized is important to him/her
questions.english:
A very organized person I'd like to talk about is my supervisor. They are a good person, and what stands out to me is how they manage research work, rather than just how tidy their desk looks.

They keep a short list of priorities and arrange regular discussions with students. Before a meeting, they ask us to write down the main problem, what we've tried and what kind of help we need. That stops the conversation from becoming too vague.

I noticed this quality while preparing a robotics project. There were several things to check, and it was easy to jump between them without making progress. My supervisor helped us put the tasks in a sensible order and keep track of the results.

Being organized matters to them because research involves uncertainty. A good plan can't guarantee success, but it can prevent unnecessary confusion. I admire this approach because I'm quite rational myself, and I prefer to understand what I'm doing and why. It's a habit I'd like to develop further.
questions.chinese:
我想讲的一位很有条理的人是我的导师。导师人很好。让我印象深刻的是导师安排研究工作的方式，而不只是桌面是否整洁。

导师会保留一份简短的优先事项清单，并定期与学生讨论。开会前，导师会让我们写下主要问题、尝试过什么，以及需要什么帮助。这样，讨论就不会太笼统。

我在准备机器人项目时注意到了这种特质。当时有几件事需要检查，很容易在它们之间来回切换，却没有进展。导师帮助我们把任务按合理顺序排列，并记录结果。

有条理对导师很重要，因为研究包含不确定性。好的计划不能保证成功，但能避免不必要的混乱。我欣赏这种方式，因为我自己也比较理性，喜欢理解正在做什么以及为什么做。这也是我想进一步培养的习惯。
pending: 导师安排会议、要求准备清单和指导项目等细节是候选

questions.title: 嘈杂地
questions.text:
Describe a noisy place you have been to
You should say:
Where it is
When you went there
What you did there
And explain why you feel it’s a noisy place
questions.english:
A noisy place I can describe is a railway station during my European trip in June. I travelled to Europe on my own to attend an academic conference, and I also visited Vienna and Budapest.

I was waiting for a train and trying to keep track of the departure information. There were announcements over the speakers, people talking and the sound of luggage being pulled across the floor. Trains arriving and leaving added another layer of noise.

The place felt noisy because several different sounds were happening at the same time. It was harder to concentrate than it would have been in a quiet room. I would occasionally look at the display again to make sure I hadn't missed anything important.

I don't think the noise was completely avoidable, because a station is a busy public place. Still, clear announcements and a quieter waiting area would make it more comfortable. As someone who is usually fairly quiet, I'd prefer to have a place where I could sit and think without so many distractions.
questions.chinese:
我可以描述一个嘈杂的地方，是六月欧洲旅行中的火车站。我独自赴欧洲参加学术会议，也参观了维也纳和布达佩斯。

我当时等火车，并试图留意发车信息。有广播、交谈声，以及行李箱在地面拖动的声音。列车到站和离站又增加了一层噪声。

这里显得嘈杂，是因为几种不同声音同时发生。相比安静的房间，我更难集中注意力。我会时不时再看显示屏，确认没有漏掉重要信息。

我认为这些声音不可能完全避免，因为车站是繁忙的公共场所。不过，清晰的广播和更安静的候车区会让体验更舒适。我通常比较安静，因此更希望有一个能坐下来思考、少受干扰的地方。
pending: 等火车事实已确认；具体车站、嘈杂程度及查看屏幕等活动是候选，不指定聊天城市

questions.title: 有条理的人
questions.text: Do you think it is important for managers to be well organized?
questions.english: Yes, because a manager's decisions affect other people's work. If priorities and deadlines are unclear, the whole team may waste time or repeat tasks. An organized manager can assign responsibilities and notice problems early. Still, organization shouldn't mean controlling every detail. Team members need enough freedom to handle their own work and suggest better approaches.
questions.chinese: 是的，因为经理的决定影响其他人的工作。优先事项和截止时间不明确时，团队可能浪费时间或重复任务。有条理的经理能分配责任、及早发现问题。但有条理不等于控制每个细节。团队成员需要足够自由来处理工作、提出更好方法。

questions.title: 有条理的人
questions.text: Should parents teach their children to be organized?
questions.english: Parents can start with simple habits, such as putting toys away and preparing a schoolbag before bed. Showing children what to do usually works better than only giving instructions. The aim should be to make daily life easier, not to demand perfect tidiness. Children also need opportunities to make mistakes and gradually take responsibility themselves.
questions.chinese: 家长可以从简单习惯开始，比如收好玩具、睡前准备书包。向孩子示范通常比只发指令更有效。目标应是让日常生活更方便，而不是要求完美整洁。孩子也需要犯错的机会，逐步自己承担责任。

questions.title: 有条理的人
questions.text: What can people do to become more organized?
questions.english: A useful first step is to write down tasks instead of trying to remember everything. People can then choose their main priorities and set realistic deadlines. Keeping important files in clear folders also helps. I would start with a small system that is easy to maintain, because a complicated planning tool can become another source of work.
questions.chinese: 有用的第一步是写下任务，而不是努力记住一切。然后选择主要优先事项、设定现实的截止时间。把重要文件放在清晰的文件夹里也有帮助。我会从容易维护的小系统开始，因为复杂的规划工具可能变成另一项工作。

questions.text: Are organized people more likely to be successful at work or in their studies?
questions.english: They often have an advantage because they can manage deadlines and avoid forgetting important tasks. That leaves more time for careful work or study. However, being organized doesn't replace knowledge, creativity, or effort. A neat timetable is useful only if someone actually follows it and adjusts it when necessary. questions.text: How can people consider others' feelings when chatting in public?

questions.title: 嘈杂地
questions.text: How would people usually respond to noises in your country?
questions.english: In China, I think reactions vary with the setting. People may accept noise in markets or busy restaurants, but feel annoyed by loud phone calls on public transport. Some ignore it, while others politely ask for quiet. Repeated noise near someone's home may lead to a complaint. So context and duration make a big difference.
questions.chinese: 在中国，我认为反应随场景不同。人们可能接受市场或繁忙餐馆里的噪声，却对公共交通上大声打电话感到烦。有些人忽略，有些礼貌地请求安静。住所附近反复的噪声可能导致投诉。因此，场景与持续时间影响很大。

questions.title: 嘈杂地
questions.text: Which area is exposed to noise more, the city or the countryside?
questions.english: Cities generally have more continuous noise because traffic, construction, and businesses are close together. In the countryside, there are usually fewer sources operating at the same time. However, rural places aren't always silent. Farm machinery or a local celebration can be quite loud. The main difference is often the frequency and concentration of noise rather than its existence.
questions.chinese: 城市通常有更多持续噪声，因为交通、施工和商家集中在一起。乡村同时运转的噪声源通常较少，但乡村并非总是安静。农业机械或当地庆祝活动也能很响。主要差别往往是噪声的频率和集中程度，而非有没有噪声。

questions.text: What kinds of noises are there in our life?

questions.title: 嘈杂地
questions.text: Should children not be allowed to make noise under any circumstances?
questions.english: No, a complete ban would be unreasonable. Children make noise when they play, learn, or express excitement, and that is a normal part of growing up. They should learn to be quiet in places like libraries, though. Adults can explain the difference between settings and provide spaces where energetic play is welcome, instead of expecting silence everywhere.

questions.text: Do you think it is good for children to make noise?

I would encourage children to express themselves while teaching them to notice their surroundings and respect situations that call for quiet.
